In mathematics, the '''supergolden ratio''' is a  geometrical [[aspect ratio|proportion]], given by the unique real [[polynomial root|solution]] of the equation {{nowrap|{{math|1=''x''{{isup|3}} = ''x''{{isup|2}} + 1}}.}} Its decimal expansion begins with {{math|{{val|1.465571231876768|end=...}} }} {{OEIS|A092526}}.<!-- PLEASE DO NOT add additional digits to the value of ψ in this equation; there is a long-standing consensus that additional digits do not add to understanding. Thank you.-->

The name ''supergolden ratio'' is by analogy with the [[golden ratio]], the positive solution of the equation {{math|1=''x''{{isup|2}} = ''x'' + 1.}}

==Definition==
[[File:Supergolden cuboid.svg |thumb|upright=1.25 |ψ = {{sfrac|a|b}} = {{sfrac|a+c|a}} = {{sfrac|b|c}}. For b = 1 the boxes have volumes {{math|1=ψ{{isup|3}} = ψ{{isup|2}} (red) + 1 (green).}}]]

Three quantities {{math|a > b > c > 0}} are in the supergolden ratio if
<math display="block">\frac{a+c}{a}=\frac{a}{b}=\frac{b}{c} </math>
This common ratio is commonly denoted {{tmath|\psi.}}

Substituting {{tmath|1=b=\psi c}} and {{tmath|1=a=\psi b =\psi^2 c}} in the first fraction,
<math display=block>\psi =\frac{c(\psi^2 +1)}{\psi^2 c}.</math> It follows that the supergolden ratio is the unique real solution of the [[cubic equation]] {{tmath|1=\psi^3 -\psi^2 -1 =0}}.

The [[Minimal polynomial (field theory)|minimal polynomial]] for the reciprocal root is the [[depressed cubic]] {{tmath|x^3 +x -1}},<ref>{{OEIS|A263719}}</ref> thus the simplest solution with [[Cubic equation#Cardano's formula|Cardano's formula]],
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 w_{1,2} &=\left( 1 \pm \frac{1}{3} \sqrt{ \frac{31}{3}} \right) /2 \\
 1 /\psi &=\sqrt[3]{w_1} +\sqrt[3]{w_2} \end{align}</math>

or, using the [[Cubic equation#Trigonometric and hyperbolic solutions|hyperbolic sine]],
<math display=block>1 /\psi =\frac{2}{ \sqrt{3}} \sinh \left( \frac{1}{3} \operatorname{arsinh} \left( \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2} \right) \right).</math>

[[File:Supergolden triangle.png |thumb |A triangle with side lengths {{math|ψ, 1,}} and {{math|1 ∕ ψ}} has an angle of exactly 120 degrees.<ref>{{OEIS|A092526}}</ref>]]

{{tmath|1 /\psi}} is the superstable [[Fixed-point iteration|fixed point]] of the [[Newton's method]] iteration {{tmath|x \gets (2x^3 +1) /(3x^2 +1)}}.

Dividing the defining trinomial {{tmath|x^3 -x^2 -1}} by {{tmath|x -\psi}} one obtains {{tmath|x^2 +x /\psi^2 +1 /\psi}}, and the [[Conjugate element (field theory)|conjugate elements]] of {{tmath|\psi}} are
<math display=block>x_{1,2} = \left( -1 \pm i \sqrt{4 \psi^2 + 3} \right) /2 \psi^2 ,</math>
with {{tmath|1=x_1 +x_2 = 1 -\psi}} and {{tmath|1=x_1x_2 =1 /\psi}}.

The iteration <math>x \gets \sqrt[3]{\phantom{|} 1 +x^2}</math> results in the [[Nested radical#Infinitely nested radicals|continued radical]]&nbsp;{{efn |{{math|1={{radic|x|m/n}} = x{{sup|n/m}} }} }}
<math display=block> \psi^3 -1 =\psi^2 =\sqrt[3/2]{1 +\sqrt[3/2]{1 +\sqrt[3/2]{\phantom{|} 1 +\cdots}}} </math>

Better convergence is attained by using relation <math> y^3 =y(1-2y) +3 \,</math> with real zero {{tmath|\psi^2 -1}}. Divide both sides by {{tmath|y}}, and substitute <math>\psi^{-3} =1/(y+2) \,\text{ for }\, 3/y -2y.</math> This gives the iteration <math> y \gets \sqrt{1 +\tfrac{1}{2+y}},</math> and the continued reciprocal square root
<math display=block> \psi^2 -1=\sqrt{1 +\cfrac{1}{2+\sqrt{1 +\cfrac{1}{2+\sqrt{1 +\cfrac{1}{2 +\ddots}}}}}} </math>

==Properties==
[[File:SuperGoldenSquare_6.png |thumb|upright=1.25 |Rectangles in aspect ratios {{math|ψ, ψ{{sup|2}} }} and {{math|ψ{{sup|3}} }} (from left to right) tile the square.]]

The supergolden ratio can be expressed in terms of itself in many different ways, for example as fractions
<math display=block> 2\psi -1 =\frac{\psi^2 +2}{\psi^2} =\frac{\psi^3 +1}{\psi^3 -1} =\frac{2\psi^7 -1}{\psi^7},</math> along with
<math display=block> \begin{align}
 1 +\psi^{-1} &=\frac{\psi^2 +2}{\psi +1} =\frac{2\psi^3 -1}{\psi^3} \\
 1 +\psi^{-3} &=\frac{\psi^2 +2}{\psi^2 +1} \\
 1 +\psi^{-5} &=\frac{\psi +1}{\psi^2} \\
 =\psi^2 -1 &=\frac{\psi^7 +1}{\psi^7 -1} \\
 \psi^4 -1 &=\frac{\psi^2 +2}{\psi^2 -1} \\
 \psi^6 -1 &=\frac{\psi^2 +2}{\psi -1}.\end{align} </math>

Similarly as infinite [[geometric series]]
<math display=block> \begin{align}
 \psi^3 &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-n} \\
 \frac{\psi^2}{\psi^2 -1} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-2n} \\
 \psi &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-3n} \\
 \frac{\psi}{\psi^2 -1} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-4n} \\
 \frac{1}{3 -\psi^2} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-5n} \\
 \frac{1}{\psi^2 -1} +\frac{1}{\psi^2 +2} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-6n} \\
 \frac{\psi^2}{2} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \psi^{-7n}.\end{align}</math>
Additionally, <math>\sum_{n=0}^{7} \psi^{-n} = 3.</math>

For every integer {{tmath|n}} one has
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \psi^n &=\psi^{n-1} +\psi^{n-3} \\
 &=\psi^{n-2} +\psi^{n-3} +\psi^{n-4} \\
 &=\psi^{n-2} +2\psi^{n-4} +\psi^{n-6}
\end{align}</math>
from this an infinite number of further relations can be found.

Argument {{tmath|1=\theta =\arcsec(2\psi^{4})}} satisfies the identity {{tmath|1=\tan(\theta) -4\sin(\theta) =3\sqrt{{(}}3{{)}}}}.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4600807/ |title=On the tribonacci constant with cos(2πk/11), plastic constant with cos(2πk/23), and others |last=Piezas III |first=Tito |date=Dec 18, 2022 |website=Mathematics stack exchange |access-date=June 11, 2024}}</ref>

[[Simple continued fraction|Continued fraction]] pattern of a few low powers
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \psi^{-1} &=[0;1,2,6,1,3,5,4,22,...] \approx 0.6823 \;(\tfrac{13}{19}) \\
 \psi^0 &=[1] \\
 \psi^1 &=[1;2,6,1,3,5,4,22,1,...] \approx 1.4656 \;(\tfrac{22}{15}) \\
 \psi^2 &=[2;6,1,3,5,4,22,1,1,...] \approx 2.1479 \;(\tfrac{15}{7}) \\
 \psi^3 &=[3;6,1,3,5,4,22,1,1,...] \approx 3.1479 \;(\tfrac{22}{7}) \\
 \psi^4 &=[4;1,1,1,1,2,2,1,2,2,...] \approx 4.6135 \;(\tfrac{60}{13}) \\
 \psi^5 &=[6;1,3,5,4,22,1,1,4,...] \approx 6.7614 \;(\tfrac{115}{17})
\end{align}</math>

Notably, the continued fraction of {{tmath|\psi^2 }} begins as [[permutation]] of the first six natural numbers; the next term is equal to their {{nowrap|sum + 1.}}

As derived from its continued fraction expansion, the simplest rational approximations of {{tmath|\psi}} are:
<math display=block>\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{19}{13},\tfrac{22}{15},\tfrac{85}{58},\tfrac{277}{189},\tfrac{447}{305},\tfrac{1873}{1278},\tfrac{41653}{28421},\tfrac{43526}{29699},\tfrac{85179}{58120}, \ldots</math>

[[File:Supergolden Newton map.svg |thumb|upright=1.25 |[[Newton's method]] for {{math|1=p(z) = z{{isup|3}} − z{{isup|2}} − 1:}} {{nowrap|{{math|ψ}} (right)}} and its complex conjugates at the nuclei of their [[Attractor#Basins_of_attraction|basins of attraction]]. [[Julia set]] of the Newton map in orange, with unit circle and real curve for reference.]]

The supergolden ratio is the fourth smallest [[Pisot number]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Panju |first=Maysum |date=2011 |title=A systematic construction of almost integers |url=https://mathreview.uwaterloo.ca/archive/voli/2/panju.pdf |journal=The Waterloo Mathematics Review |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=35–43}}</ref> By definition of these numbers, the [[Absolute value#Complex numbers|absolute value]] <math>1 /\sqrt{\psi}</math> of the algebraic conjugates is smaller than 1, thus powers of {{tmath|\psi}} generate [[almost integer]]s.
For example: <math> \psi^{11} =67.000222765...</math> {{tmath|\approx 67 +1/4489}}. After eleven rotation steps the [[Phase (waves)|phase]]s of the inward spiraling conjugate pair &ndash; initially close to {{tmath|\pm 13 \pi/22}} &ndash; nearly align with the imaginary axis.

The [[Minimal polynomial (field theory)|minimal polynomial]] of the supergolden ratio {{tmath|1=m(x) =x^3 -x^2 -1}} has [[discriminant]] <math>\Delta=-31 .</math> The [[Hilbert class field]] of imaginary [[quadratic field]] <math>K = \mathbb{Q}( \sqrt{\Delta})</math> can be formed by adjoining {{tmath|\psi.}} With argument <math>\tau=(1 +\sqrt{\Delta})/2\,</math> a generator for the [[ring of integers]] of {{tmath|K}}, one has the special value of [[Dedekind eta function|Dedekind eta]] quotient
<math display=block>\psi =\frac{ e^{\pi i/24}\,\eta(\tau)}{ \sqrt{2}\,\eta(2\tau)}.</math>

Expressed in terms of the [[Weber modular function|Weber-Ramanujan class invariant G<sub>n</sub>]]&nbsp;{{efn|German Wikipedia has a table of analytical values of the {{ill|Ramanujan G-function|de|Ramanujansche g-Funktion und G-Funktion#Spezielle Werte}} for odd arguments below 47.}}
<math display=block>\psi =\frac{ \mathfrak{f} ( \sqrt{ \Delta} )}{ \sqrt{2} } =\frac{ G_{31} }{ \sqrt[4]{2} }.</math>

Properties of the related [[J-invariant#The q-expansion and moonshine|Klein j-invariant]] {{tmath|j(\tau)}} result in near identity <math>e^{\pi \sqrt{- \Delta}} \approx \left( \sqrt{2}\,\psi \right)^{24} - 24 .</math> The difference is {{math|< 1/143092}}.

The [[Modular lambda function#Lambda-star|elliptic integral singular value]]&nbsp;<ref>{{MathWorld |id=EllipticIntegralSingularValue |title=Elliptic integral singular value}}</ref> <math>k_{r} =\lambda^{*}(r)</math> for {{tmath|r{{=}}31}} has closed form expression
<math display=block>\lambda^{*}(31) =\sin ( \arcsin \left( ( \sqrt[4]{2}\,\psi)^{-12} \right) /2)</math>
(which is less than 1/10 the [[Eccentricity (mathematics)#Ellipses|eccentricity]] of the orbit of Venus).

==Narayana sequence==
{{multiple image
| total_width=320
| direction=vertical
| image_gap=6
| image1=Supergolden_Rauzy_cub.png
| caption1=A [[#matrix|Rauzy fractal]] associated with the supergolden ratio-cubed. The central tile and its three subtiles have areas in the ratios {{math|ψ{{sup|4}} : ψ{{sup|2}} : ψ : 1.}}
| image2=Supergolden_Rauzy_sqr.png
| caption2=A Rauzy fractal associated with the supergolden ratio-squared, with areas as above.
}}

Narayana's cows is a [[Constant-recursive sequence|recurrence sequence]] originating from a problem proposed by the 14th century Indian mathematician [[Narayana Pandita (mathematician)|Narayana Pandita]].<ref name="oeiscow">{{OEIS|A000930}}</ref> He asked for the number of cows and calves in a herd after 20 years, beginning with one cow in the first year, where each cow gives birth to one calf each year from the age of three onwards.

The Narayana sequence has a close connection to the [[Fibonacci sequence|Fibonacci]] and [[Padovan sequence]]s and plays an important role in data coding, cryptography and combinatorics. The number of [[Composition (combinatorics)|compositions]] of n into parts 1 and 3 is counted by the ''n''th Narayana number.

The Narayana sequence is defined by the third-order [[recurrence relation]]
<math display=block>N_n =N_{n-1} +N_{n-3} \text{ for } n >2,</math>
with initial values
<math display=block>N_0 =N_1 =N_2 =1.</math>

The first few terms are 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, 19, 28, 41, 60, 88,... {{OEIS|A000930}}.
The limit ratio between consecutive terms is the supergolden ratio:<math>\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} N_{n+1}/N_n =\psi.</math>

The first 11 indices n for which <math>N_n</math> is prime are n = 3, 4, 8, 9, 11, 16, 21, 25, 81, 6241, 25747 {{OEIS|A170954}}. The last number has 4274 decimal digits.

The sequence is extended to negative indices using
<math display=block> N_n =N_{n+3} -N_{n+2},</math>
obtaining (1), 0, 0, 1, 0,−1, 1, 1,−2, 0, 3,−2,−3, 5,...

Powers of the supergolden ratio can be written with Narayana numbers as quadratic coefficients <math display=block> \psi^n =\psi^2 N_{n-2} +\psi N_{n-4} +N_{n-3},</math> which is proved by [[mathematical induction]] on {{tmath|n.}} This relation also holds for {{tmath|n < 0.}} The order of the coefficients corresponds to the bottom row of matrix {{tmath|Q}} below.

The [[generating function]] of the Narayana sequence for non-negative {{tmath|n}} is given by
<math display=block>\frac{1}{1 -x -x^3} =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} N_n x^n \text{ for } x <\tfrac{1}{\psi}</math>

The Narayana numbers are related to sums of [[binomial coefficient]]s by
<math display=block>N_n =\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n / 3 \rfloor}{n-2k \choose k}</math>

The [[Characteristic equation (calculus)|characteristic equation]] of the recurrence is <math>x^3 -x^2 -1 =0 .</math> If the three solutions are real root {{tmath|\psi}} and conjugate pair {{tmath|\beta}} and {{tmath|\gamma}}, the Narayana numbers are given by the [[Fibonacci sequence#Binet's formula|Binet formula]]&nbsp;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lin |first=Xin| date=2021 |title=On the recurrence properties of Narayana's cows sequence |journal=[[Symmetry (journal)|Symmetry]] |volume=13 |issue=1 |article-number=149 | pages = 1–12<!-- comment to head off Citation bot from breaking this again --> |doi=10.3390/sym13010149 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2021Symm...13..149L |language=en}}</ref>
<math display=block>N_{n-1} =a \psi^n +b \beta^n +c \gamma^n ,</math>
with real {{tmath|a}} and conjugates {{tmath|b}} and {{tmath|c}} the roots of <math> 31x^3 -3x -1 =0.</math>

Since <math>\left\vert b \beta^n +c \gamma^n \right\vert < \psi^{-n/2} </math>, the number {{tmath|N_n }} is the [[nearest integer function|nearest integer]] to {{tmath| \,a\,\psi^{n+1} }}, with {{tmath|n \ge 0}} and coefficient <math> a =\psi^2 /(\psi^3 +2) =</math> {{gaps|0.41723|79879|26218|77762|14755...}}

Coefficients <math>a =b =c =1</math> result in the Binet formula for the related sequence <math>A_n =N_n +2N_{n-3} .</math>

The first few terms are 3, 1, 1, 4, 5, 6, 10, 15, 21, 31, 46, 67, 98, 144,... {{OEIS|A001609}}.

This anonymous sequence has the [[Fermat's little theorem|Fermat property]]: if p is prime, <math>A_{p} \equiv A_1 \bmod p .</math> The converse does not hold, but the small number of odd [[pseudoprime]]s <math>\,n \mid (A_n -1)</math> makes the sequence special.<ref>Studied together with the [[Perrin sequence]] in: {{cite journal |last1=Adams |first1=William |last2=Shanks |first2=Daniel |author-link2=Daniel Shanks |title=Strong primality tests that are not sufficient |journal=Math. Comp. |date=1982 |volume=39 |issue=159 |pages=255–300 |publisher=AMS |doi=10.2307/2007637 |doi-access=free |jstor=2007637}}</ref> The 8 odd composite numbers below {{math|10{{sup|8}} }} to pass the test are n = 1155, 552599, 2722611, 4822081, 10479787, 10620331, 16910355, 66342673.

[[File:Supergolden_Rauzy_ab.png |thumb|upright=1.25 |A supergolden Rauzy fractal of type a ↦ ab, with areas as above. The fractal boundary has [[Minkowski–Bouligand dimension|box-counting]] [[Fractal dimension|dimension]] 1.50]]

The Narayana numbers are obtained as integral powers {{math|''n'' > 3}} of a [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] with real [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors#Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices|eigenvalue]] {{tmath|\psi}} <ref name="oeiscow"/>
<math display=block>Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} ,</math>

<math display=block id="matrix"> Q^n =\begin{pmatrix} N_n & N_{n-2} & N_{n-1} \\ N_{n-1} & N_{n-3} & N_{n-2} \\ N_{n-2} & N_{n-4} & N_{n-3} \end{pmatrix}</math>

The [[Trace (linear algebra)#Relationship to eigenvalues|trace]] of {{tmath|Q^n }} gives the above {{tmath|A_n }}.

Alternatively, {{tmath|Q}} can be interpreted as [[incidence matrix]] for a [[Morphic word#D0L system|D0L]] [[L-system|Lindenmayer system]] on the alphabet {{tmath|\{a,b,c\} }} with corresponding  [[Semi-Thue system|substitution rule]]
<math display=block>\begin{cases}
 a \;\mapsto \;ab \\
 b \;\mapsto \;c \\
 c \;\mapsto \;a \end{cases}</math>
and initiator {{tmath|w_0{{=}}b}}. The series of words {{tmath|w_n}} produced by iterating the substitution have lengths <math> l(w_n) =N_n </math>. The number of {{math|''c'', ''b'' and ''a's''}} in each word is equal to successive Narayana numbers. Associated to this string rewriting process is a [[Compact space|compact]] set composed of [[Self-similarity|self-similar]] tiles called the [[Rauzy fractal]], that visualizes the [[Combinatorics on words|combinatorial]] information contained in a multiple-generation three-letter sequence.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Siegel |first1=Anne |last2=Thuswaldner |first2=Jörg M. |date=2009 |title=Topological properties of Rauzy fractals |url=http://numdam.org/item/MSMF_2009_2_118__1_0/ |journal=Mémoires de la Société Mathématique de France |volume=118 |series=2 |pages=1–140 |doi=10.24033/msmf.430}}</ref>

The ratio between the number of digits in successive strings for the binary version of the [[look-and-say sequence]] converges to {{tmath|\psi}}.<ref>{{OEIS|A049194}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Sillke |first=Torsten |date=April 7, 1993 |title=The binary form of Conway's sequence |url=https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~sillke/SEQUENCES/series001 |website=Homepage of Torsten Sillke |location=Faculty of Mathematics |publisher=Universität Bielefeld |access-date=September 10, 2026 }}</ref>

==Geometry==
===Psi-quad substitution tiling===
{{multiple image
| total_width = 390
| direction   = horizontal
| image1      = Psiquad.svg
| caption1    = Psi-quad substitution tiling.
| image2      = Supergolden.svg
| caption2    = Supergolden fractal triangle.
}}
In the complex plane, if {{tmath|\psi}} is a non-real root of <math> \psi^3 -\psi^2 -1 =0 </math>, then the vertices of a self-similar quadrilateral tiling (the ''psi-quad'' [[substitution tiling]]) can be taken as the six points <math> \psi^0, \psi^1, \psi^2, \psi^3, \psi^4, -\psi^2 </math>. The iterated boundary is the supergolden fractal triangle, which has [[Hausdorff dimension]] <math> d_{\partial} =\frac{2 \log \zeta}{\log \psi}</math>, where {{tmath|\zeta}} is the real root of <math> \zeta^7 -2\zeta^2 -1 =0 </math>, so numerically {{tmath| d_{\partial} \approx 1.0295240599 }}.

===Supergolden rectangle===
[[File:Supergolden_ratio.svg |thumb|upright=1.5 |Nested supergolden rectangles with perpendicular diagonals and side lengths in powers of {{math|ψ}}.]]

A supergolden rectangle is a [[rectangle]] whose side lengths are in a {{tmath|\psi:1}} ratio. Compared to the [[golden rectangle]], the supergolden rectangle has one more degree of [[self-similarity]].

Given a rectangle of height {{math|1}}, length {{tmath|\psi}} and diagonal length <math>\sqrt{\psi^3}</math> (according to <math>1 +\psi^2 =\psi^3</math>). The triangles on the diagonal have [[Altitude (triangle)|altitude]]s <math>1 /\sqrt{\psi}\,;</math> each perpendicular foot divides the diagonal in ratio {{tmath|\psi^2}}.

On the left-hand side, cut off a square of side length {{math|1}} and mark the intersection with the falling diagonal. The remaining rectangle now has [[aspect ratio]] <math>\psi^2 :1</math> (according to <math>\psi -1 =\psi^{-2}</math>). Divide the original rectangle into four parts by a second, horizontal cut passing through the intersection point.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Crilly |first=Tony |date=1994 |title=A supergolden rectangle |journal=[[The Mathematical Gazette]] |volume=78 |issue=483 |pages=320–325 |doi=10.2307/3620208 |jstor=3620208 |s2cid=125782726 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Koshy |first=Thomas |title=Fibonacci and Lucas numbers with applications |date=2017 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |edition=2 |doi=10.1002/9781118033067 |isbn=978-0-471-39969-8 |language=en}}</ref>

The rectangle below the diagonal has aspect ratio {{tmath|\psi^3}}, the other three are all supergolden rectangles, with a fourth one between the feet of the altitudes. The parent rectangle and the four scaled copies have linear sizes in the ratios <math>\psi^3 :\psi^2 :\psi :\psi^2 -1 :1.</math> It follows from the [[theorem of the gnomon]] that the areas of the two rectangles opposite the diagonal are equal.

In the supergolden rectangle above the diagonal, the process is repeated at a scale of {{tmath|1:\psi^2}}.

===Supergolden spiral===
[[File:Supergolden_spiral.svg |thumb |upright=1.5 |Supergolden spirals with different initial radii on a {{math|ψ}}− rectangle.]]
A supergolden spiral is a [[logarithmic spiral]] that gets wider by a factor of {{tmath|\psi}} for every quarter turn. It is described by the [[polar equation]] <math>r( \theta) =a \exp(k \theta),</math> with initial radius {{tmath|a}} and parameter <math>k =\frac{2}{\pi} \ln( \psi).</math> If drawn on a supergolden rectangle, the spiral has its pole at the foot of altitude of a triangle on the diagonal and passes through vertices of rectangles with aspect ratio {{tmath|\psi}} which are perpendicularly aligned and successively scaled by a factor {{tmath|\psi^{-1}.}}

{{br}}

==See also==
Solutions of equations similar to <math>x^3 =x^2 +1</math>:
* [[Golden ratio]] – the positive solution of the equation <math>x^2 =x +1</math>
* [[Plastic ratio]] – the real solution of the equation <math>x^3 =x +1</math>
* [[Supersilver ratio]] – the real solution of the equation <math>x^3 =2x^2 +1</math>
